New York police officers have shot dead a 26-year-old man, identified as Omatoyo Neverson, after a suspected abduction report triggered a vehicle chase and confrontation on the Belt Parkway in Brooklyn. The incident occurred shortly before 7:30 pm on Saturday after two people called emergency services to report a possible abduction involving a woman inside a white van in the Coney Island neighbourhood. According to NBC New York, in a now updated report on Monday, the callers alerted nearby police officers after reporting that a woman was screaming and apparently struggling inside the vehicle. Speaking at a press briefing, NYPD Assistant Chief Charles Minch said the male caller reported seeing the woman inside the van, saying, “There’s a girl kicking and screaming in there.” The female caller, meanwhile, told emergency operators that she heard the woman repeatedly shouting, “Let me go!” Minch said the callers subsequently spotted officers in a marked police vehicle and alerted them to the suspected abduction. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources When the officers approached the white van, however, the driver allegedly drove onto the sidewalk and sped away. Police broadcast the vehicle’s description and registration details over their radio channels before officers located it in heavy traffic on the eastbound Belt Parkway in Sheepshead Bay. According to the police account, officers approached the van, ordered the driver to get out and broke its front passenger-side window when he failed to comply. Minch said the driver subsequently began moving the vehicle forwards and backwards, striking police and civilian vehicles. “The driver began to drive forwards and backwards, ramming both police and occupied civilian vehicles indiscriminately on the Belt Parkway,” he said. Officers then discharged their firearms and struck the driver,” Minch said. The officers removed the driver from the van, called an ambulance and performed cardiopulmonary resuscitation before he was taken to NYU Langone Hospital–Brooklyn, where he was pronounced dead. Police later identified the deceased as Neverson, 26, of Canarsie, Brooklyn. However, subsequent investigations established that the person initially believed to be a kidnapped girl was an adult woman who had escaped from the van before officers arrived. “The female is an adult and was not injured,” Minch said, adding that she confirmed she had been inside the van and had been screaming before leaving the vehicle. “At this point, we believe that the screaming was in relation to a domestic dispute,” he added. Minch also disclosed that Neverson was wanted in connection with an unlawful imprisonment case reported the previous month and a domestic assault earlier in November. Police said the woman found in the van was the victim in both cases. The fatal shooting was captured on police body-worn cameras and is being investigated by the NYPD’s Force Investigation Unit. The New York State Attorney General’s Office of Special Investigation is also expected to review the incident, in line with its responsibility to investigate deaths involving police officers. The shooting forced the temporary closure of parts of the Belt Parkway as investigators examined the scene.
